Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will embark on an official visit to Qatar from 27 to 29 September 2026
articles.full_content:
Union Finance Minister will attend the 11th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) during the visit The Union Finance Minister Smt. Sitharaman will also hold important bilateral meetings with the AIIB President and her counterparts including from Jordan, Switzerland, Algeria, Saudi Arabia, and Nepal
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will embark on an official visit to Qatar from 27 th to 29 th September, 2026. The Union Finance Minister is leading the delegation comprising of Ministry of Finance officials.
During the visit, Smt. Sitharaman will attend the 11 th Annual Meeting of Board of Governors of Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) scheduled in Doha on 28 th September 2026, besides other important bilateral meetings with the AIIB President and her counterparts from Jordan, Switzerland, Algeria, Saudi Arabia, and Nepal.
In the Annual Meeting of AIIB, the Union Finance Minister will attend as the Indian Governor to the AIIB. India is the second largest shareholder of the bank.
As part of the official visit, the Union Finance Minister is expected to call-on the leadership of the Government of Qatar, and also engage with Qatari business leaders and investors.
About AIIB and Annual Meetings
The AIIB Annual Meeting witnesses participation of delegations from member countries, and other international organisations. As a multilateral development bank, AIIB is focused on developing sustainable infrastructure in Asia and in promoting investments in infrastructure and other productive sectors with the aim to foster sustainable economic development, create wealth and improve infrastructure connectivity.

ICAR Institutes Promote Cleanliness and Sustainable Waste Management
articles.full_content:
As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva activities, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) organised awareness and cleanliness initiatives focused on post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness, clean public spaces and responsible waste management at ICAR institutions. The initiatives aimed to promote environmental protection, safe practices and community participation in maintaining clean surroundings after Ganesh Visarjan.
An awareness programme on post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness was organised at a local Ganesh pandal, where participants were sensitised about the use of eco-friendly clay idols and advised to avoid immersion of Plaster of Paris idols and idols containing harmful chemical colours in drinking water tanks. Participants were encouraged to use designated immersion sites and avoid immersing idols and Puja Samagri in natural water bodies. Emphasis was also laid on proper collection and disposal of flowers, Puja Samagri, plastic, thermocol and other decorative waste.
The programme also highlighted the importance of maintaining cleanliness at immersion sites, preventing littering and following safety precautions near water bodies. The areas surrounding the local Ganesh pandal were cleaned, with garbage collected and segregated to facilitate safe and responsible waste management. The initiative highlighted the importance of collective responsibility and community participation in protecting water resources and maintaining clean public spaces.
As part of the activities, biodegradable offerings including flowers and other Puja Samagri were collected and segregated at ICAR-NISA, Ranchi, Jharkhand , and ICAR-CIRCOT, Mumbai, Maharashtra . The compostable material was processed at composting facilities for preparation of organic manure. The initiative resulted in the cleaning and segregation of biodegradable waste generated during Ganesh Visarjan and its conversion into a useful resource through composting.
The activities contributed to promoting awareness on cleanliness, sanitation, environmental protection and responsible waste management, while encouraging the adoption of clean, safe and environmentally responsible practices during and after Ganesh Visarjan.

70,000 Rural Youth to Begin Skill Training Under DDU-GKY 2.0 Across States/UTs from October 2026
articles.full_content:
Ministry of Rural Development Accelerates DDU-GKY 2.0 Rollout Across States/UTs
The Ministry of Rural Development is set to roll out Deen Dayal Upadhyaya- Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) 2.0 training batches across most of the States/UTs from October 2026.
As per the DDU-GKY 2.0 portal ( https://kaushal.rural.gov.in ) allocations of 5.6 lakh targets towards more than 1,200 projects to the Project Implementation Agencies (PIAs) have been done by 24 States/UTs. Other States are in the advanced stages of target allocations. Across the country in 24 States/UTs, 2,015 batches involving around 70,000 rural youth are expected to commence their training in October 2026.
DDU-GKY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme providing placement linked skill training to poor rural youth. Duration of the training varies from 3 months to 12 months. All the 31 participating States/UTs have been allocated more than 9 lakhs targets under the DDU-GKY 2.0 for 2-year period 2026-28. States/UTs have to mobilise rural youth and to organise placement linked skill training, as per demand, in PPP mode, in National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF) aligned courses, enabling sustained employability of the beneficiaries. The Ministry emphasised that this is a crucial phase for State/UT action and called upon implementing States/UTs to accelerate the allocation of targets to Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) and to commence batches as per envisaged timelines. States/UTs are supposed to ensure allocation of targets to PIAs for commencement of trainings latest by 31 October 2026.
Review meetings in phases are being held with the States/UTs to gather momentum in the processes leading to batch commencements.

9th India International Water Week 2026 Concludes with Focus on Climate-Resilient Water Management and Sustainable Water Services
articles.full_content:
Shri C. R. Patil Calls for Collective Action to Strengthen Climate-Resilient and Sustainable Water Management at IIWW 2026 IIWW 2026 Brings Together Global Water Community to Advance Innovation, Knowledge and Sustainable WASH Solutions India International WASH Conference Highlights Community-Led Approaches, Digital Innovation and Stronger Institutions for Sustainable Water Services
The 9 th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026 concluded today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, with the Valedictory Ceremony chaired by Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil. Held from September 22–25 under the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management”, the deliberations brought together policymakers, government officials, international organisations, development partners, researchers, academia, industry, water-sector practitioners, innovators and young professionals to discuss emerging challenges and solutions for water security.
The valedictory session was graced by Ministers of State for Jal Shakti; Shri V. Somanna, Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Smt. Archana Varma, Director General, National Mission for Clean Ganga, Shri Rajeev Kumar Mital, AS & MD, NJJM, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Chairman, Central Water Commission, Shri Anupam Prasad, and Director General, National Water Development Agency, Shri Baleshwar Thakur.
Addressing the gathering, Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti underscored that IIWW 2026 provided a platform for governments, experts, institutions, academia, industry and youth to deliberate on climate-resilient water management. He highlighted three key takeaways: people’s participation in water conservation, taking science and technology to the ground, and strengthening international and institutional cooperation. Highlighting the Jal Jeevan Mission’s impact since its launch in 2019, he said expanded access to household tap water has contributed to improved health, dignity and quality of life in rural communities, while reducing the time and effort spent by women in fetching water. Referring to a WHO assessment, he said that improved access to safe drinking water under the Mission has the potential to prevent a significant number of deaths among children and reduce the health burden associated with unsafe water. He stressed that the next phase of JJM must focus on ensuring adequate, regular, safe and sustainable drinking water services, with community participation, source sustainability and appropriate technology central to sustaining these gains.

Ministry of New & Renewable Energy Gears Up for Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
Ministry and its CPSUs and Autonomous Institutes Undertake Activities for Institutionalising Swachhata and Minimising Pendency
The preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6 is underway in the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE). Launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), the campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata and minimising pendency in Government offices. It is being implemented in the ministry along with its two CPSUs and three Autonomous Institutes.
The CPSUs include Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Ltd. (IREDA) and Solar Energy Corporation of India Ltd. (SECI), and Autonomous Institutes include National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) and Sardar Swarn Singh National Institute of Bio Energy (SSS-NIBE).
The Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 will commence from 2nd October, 2026, during which concerted efforts will be made to achieve the targets identified during the Preparatory Phase and further institutionalise Swachhata, efficient record management and timely disposal of pendency across the Ministry and its PSUs/Institutions.
During the preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6, the following activities are being undertaken by the Ministry and its PSUs/Institutions:
i. Identification and disposal of pendency under various parameters.
ii. Review, categorisation and weeding out of physical records as per extant guidelines.
iii. Conduct of cleanliness campaigns for maintaining cleanliness in the Ministry and its PSUs and Autonomous Institutes.
iv. Identification and segregation of e-waste as per MoEFCC guidelines for target setting during the Implementation Phase.
The Ministry and its PSUs/Institutions actively participated in Special Campaign 5 last year, with substantial progress recorded across key areas, including Public Grievances, Public Grievance Appeals, review of physical files and e-files, and cleanliness campaigns. During the Campaign, 725 targeted e-files were reviewed, while significant progress was also made in the disposal of references received from Members of Parliament. Further, 8 out of 9 targeted cleanliness campaigns were conducted, contributing to a cleaner and more productive workplace.
The Preparatory Phase of #SpecialCampaign6 is underway at the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE), along with its 2 PSUs—IREDA & SECI—and 3 Autonomous Institutes—NISE, NIWE & SSS-NIBE, as part of the Government’s continued efforts to institutionalise Swachhata and minimise pendency in Government offices. The Implementation Phase will be undertaken from 2nd October to 31st October 2026. This year, the campaign places special emphasis on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste, along with cleanliness drives and the timely disposal of pending matters. Shillong Vartalap Highlights Public Awareness and Coordinated Action on Solid Waste Management Rules 2026
articles.full_content:
Dr Ampareen Lyngdoh Calls for Clear Communication and Coordinated Action for Effective Implementation
Greater public awareness, sustained media outreach and coordinated action among government agencies, Urban Local Bodies, Pollution Control Boards and citizens were emphasised for effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026. Speaking at a Vartalap – Media Workshop held in Shillong in the spirit of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, Dr. Mazel Ampareen Lyngdoh, Member of Legislative Assembly from 16-East Shillong and Adviser to the Government of Meghalaya, called for clear and accessible communication of the Rules to strengthen public understanding and participation.
Organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Shillong, in coordination with the Urban Affairs Department, Government of Meghalaya, the Vartalap brought together government officials, technical agencies, Urban Local Bodies and the media to discuss the new Rules, implementation timelines and ways to communicate their provisions effectively to the public.
The Vartalap was held as part of the nationwide advocacy campaign for dissemination of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026. The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has extended support to the campaign and is working with the Urban Affairs Department and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) on an appropriate media and dissemination strategy.
Appreciating the initiative, Dr. Lyngdoh commended PIB Shillong for bringing government departments, Urban Local Bodies, technical agencies and the media together on a common platform to discuss an issue of direct public importance. She also appreciated the Urban Affairs Department for its coordination and continued efforts to strengthen waste-management systems in the State.
She emphasised the need for officials to have a clear understanding of their responsibilities and communicate technical provisions in a manner that is accessible to communities. She also called for greater orientation of legislators and elected representatives on the new Rules, enabling them to engage effectively with the administration and the public. The media, she said, can play an important role in keeping citizens informed about implementation, challenges and measures being undertaken.
Reflecting on Meghalaya’s progress since 2014, Dr. Lyngdoh recalled that the State did not have a Project Management Unit (PMU) for urban sanitation at the time and communities largely relied on indigenous practices to address waste-related issues. She appreciated the Urban Affairs Department, PMU, Urban Local Bodies and municipal engineers for taking forward initiatives relating to waste management, sewage treatment and rainwater management.
Shri P. K. Boro, Director, Urban Affairs Department, Government of Meghalaya, outlined the State’s approach to urban waste management and initiatives being undertaken by the Department and Urban Local Bodies.
Shri W. R. Kharkrang, Chief Environmental Engineer, Meghalaya State Po
